item.title: Week 6 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our best bets for Sunday's games
item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 6 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 6 of the NFL season began with a Denver Broncos 17-14 overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks. The Broncos blew an 11-point fourth-quarter lead, but held on, thanks to two Sam Darnold interceptions.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Corbie Craig, Michael Fiddle, Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 6 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-2.5, 42.5) in London

Pond: Brenton Strange might be the hottest tight end in the NFL not named Trey McBride right now.

After collecting just seven receptions for 72 yards in Jacksonville's first three games, the Penn State product has caught fire, racking up 14 catches on 16 targets for 163 yards in the Jaguars' back-to-back wins against Cincinnati and Philadelphia. He also boasted a team-best 26.2% target share in those wins.

Now, Strange and Jacksonville face a Texans defense that has amassed 20 sacks, including a league-high 7 from Will Anderson Jr. The Texans are third in sack percentage and 10th in total pressures.

Lawrence is going to face the heat from Houston's nasty defensive line all day long, meaning he's going to have to get the ball out quickly to his receivers. And that's why I think Strange, who has become one of his two favorite targets — the other being Parker Washington — will prosper a third consecutive week in this showdown.

Back him to find the end zone and hit this mini ladder of receptions at plus money.

Bets: TE Brenton Strange anytime TD (+330) | 5+ receptions (+136) | 6+ receptions (+265)

New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5, 43.5)

Russell: Drake Maye has a particular set of skills. 

Maye's quarterbacking "super power" is two-fold: An ability to scramble and a nice deep-ball. During the Patriots' two-game resurgence — wins over the Bills and Raiders — Maye ran 15 times for 79 yards, and was able to hit big shots against two of the worst pass defenses in the NFL (both in the bottom-quarter of the league in Dropback EPA/Play and Success Rate). 

This week looks a little trickier, and not just because the Jets are sixth and 12th in those metrics when adjusted for garbage time and turnovers.

Will Campbell's been upgraded from doubtful, but he and right tackle Morgan Moses are both listed as questionable, on an offensive line that's given up sacks at the best of times (47 during the regular season last year, and 11 in five games this year). Until recently, that might not have been an issue against the Jets, but first-round pick David Bailey got home three times last week, and New York has 17 sacks and the seventh-best pass-rush win-rate in the league (according to ESPN). 

The Jets defense struggles against the run, but with TreVeyon Henderson out, the Patriots will have to go back to the plodding-version of their run game with Rhamondre Stevenson to take the heat off Maye. 

As for the Jets, Geno Smith must be staring at his weather app this week, with fingers crossed. The grim conditions for his two home games this season have tamped down his numbers, as his best games have come in beautiful summer weather at Tennessee and indoors against the Lions. While those defenses aren't impressive, Smith's bugaboo last season — interceptions — has been taken out of the equation this season completely. 

On what should be crisp-but-sunny autumn conditions in Foxborough, Smith could replicate the nice day he had against the Patriots defense in Week 1 last season (24-of-34, 362 yards, TD, INT) before the Raiders' offensive line (and season) fell apart. With a pass-block win-rate as good as their defensive line numbers, Smith should have the time and conditions to keep up with Maye.

Bet: Jets +7.5 (-115, DraftKings)

Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 39.5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Pond: When it comes to bare cupboards, there might not be any more empty than the one housing the Steelers' wide receivers.

Roman Wilson, Michael Pittman and Ben Skowronek are hurt. And they've all been ruled  out in Pittsburgh's clash with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

So, where does QB Aaron Rodgers turn to complement DK Metcalf down in Florida? Enter Pat Freiermuth.

The standout tight end is favorite target for Rodgers when the Steelers are deep in the opposition's territory, catching four touchdowns, including two in last week's win against the Indianapolis Colts. And things got so thin at wide receiver that Freiermuth actually lined up in the relatively foreign position to him.

Now, Rodgers, Freiermuth and the Pittsburgh offense face a Tampa Bay defense allowing the sixth-most points to tight ends this season. And that should mean chances for Freiermuth in the red zone.

I like the numbers we're getting on Freiermuth to score and to clear his receptions total. Rodgers loves him and so do we at these prices.

Bets: TE Pat Freiermuth and anytime TD (+320, BetMGM) and over 3.5 receptions (+116, FanDuel)

Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-12.5, 51.5)

Jacob: The NFL's schedule-makers didn't do any favors for the 2026 Los Angeles Rams.

First, they sent the Rams to Australia for a divisional game against one of the league's best teams (San Francisco). Then, after a Monday night home game against the Giants, the Rams hit the road for consecutive games against Denver and Philadelphia before returning home to play Buffalo.

For context, the 49ers, Broncos, Eagles and Bills posted a combined 49-19 record last season. Add several key injuries to that early-season gauntlet, and it's hardly surprising Los Angeles is off to a 2-3 start.

Now, for the first time, the Rams are home for consecutive games. And they get a cupcake opponent that has lost 18 of its last 20 games while covering the point spread just six times. Isolate the last 10 contests, and Arizona is 1-9 SU and 2-8 ATS while allowing an average of 34.7 PPG. This includes two blowout losses to the Rams (45-17 and 37-20).

Yes, Arizona got a last-minute backdoor cover three weeks ago in a 36-30 loss at San Francisco as an 8.5-point underdog. But the 49ers were in a lookahead spot that day, with games against Denver and at Seattle on deck. This week, the Cardinals face a focused — and angry — Rams squad that is eager to show why it remains a top three Super Bowl contender.

Bet the Los Angeles Rams to cover the spread at sportsbooks

Look for the Matthew Stafford-led offense to once again light up a wretched Cardinals defense. And look for L.A.'s stop unit to have its best performance since a 28-6 Week 2 win over the Giants.

Bet: Rams -12.5 (-108, BetMGM)

Pond: Like my colleague, I think the Rams are going to lay the smack down on the Cardinals after that gutting Week 5 defeat against the Bills. That should translate into Arizona finding itself in another deep hole early on in this affair.

So, what does that mean for the Cardinals and quarterback Jacoby Brissett? Air out, baby. There will be no other options.

And one of the weapons Brissett will again target often is Kendrick Bourne. Bourne finished with five receptions on eight targets for 70 yards in last weekend's defeat against the Detroit Lions. That was his best statistical performance since Arizona's Week 1 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers when he recorded eight catches on eight targets for 75 yards.

Bourne is clear WR2 behind Michael Wilson now that Marvin Harrison Jr. is with the Houston Texans, so that will open up even more opportunities to produce on a team that seemingly is always playing from behind.

I am jumping on Bourne via two ladder plays involving receptions and receiving yards. This could be a shootout and I expect him to have a big showing against the Rams.

Bets: WR Kendrick Bourne: 4+ receptions (+116) | 5+ receptions (+240) and 40+ receiving yards (+112) | 50+ receiving yards (+182) | 60+ yards (+290) at FanDuel

Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5, 42)

Fiddle: It's always hard to click the button to fade one of the hottest players in the NFL, but I think now is the right time in Kansas City.

Through four games this season — and an undefeated start — Kenneth Walker III has been the engine of the Chiefs offense. He has amassed 87 carries in those games, averaging over 21 rush attempts per game. This week, though, I think that number could drop.

The Chiefs are coming off their Week 5 bye, and head coach Andy Reid has thrived in these situational spots — he is 22-5 after the bye week. A lot of that can likely be attributed to more specific game planning and detailed play creation for the given opponent. I expect Kansas City to integrate Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen heavily into the game plan — and a few of those touches could come on gadget run plays, which would directly take from Walker.

The Chargers are likely to stack the box heavily and not afford Walker clean looks. They know wide receivers Rashee Rice and Tyquon Thornton are hurt, and Walker has been the focal point. I expect a heavy blitz rate and a run-stopping effort from L.A. defense, forcing the ball into Patrick Mahomes' hands to create with receivers in man coverage.

The angles I like here are a possible Mahomes over on his rushing yards, or Kenneth Walker under on his rushing attempts. From a market value perspective, the better odds are on Walker unders right now.

Bet: Kenneth Walker III under 19.5 rushing attempts (-115, BetMGM)

Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5, 53)

Jacob: Here are the final scores of the Cowboys' last 10 games away from Dallas: 37-32, 30-27, 44-24, 33-16, 44-30, 30-23, 34-17, 28-20, 34-31 and 34-30. All 10 games flew over the total.

Now here are the final scores of the Cowboys' last four regular season games against Green Bay: 35-31 (2017), 34-24 (2019), 31-28 (2022) and 40-40 (2025). And the last two playoff games against Green Bay: 34-31 (2016) and 48-32 (2023). All six flew over the total.

But wait, there's more: The over is 5-0 on Sunday Night Football this season. It also is 8-2 with totals that close at 50 points or higher. And Dallas — which is coming off an embarrassing 24-16 home loss to the Bucs that fell way short of the total — hasn't seen the under hit in consecutive games since Weeks 9 and 10 in 2024 (a stretch of 30 contests).

So of course for this SNF matchup I'm recommending the … under.

Call it an all-time contrarian play, but there's a correlated reason for it. Both quarterbacks — Dallas' Dak Prescott and Green Bay's Jordan Love — are among the NFL's best downfield passers. And they have to be, because neither gets any support from the running game (the Cowboys rank 30th in rushing; the Packers are dead last). 

Here's the problem: Strong, sustained winds are forecast for Sunday night in Green Bay — the kind that hamper deep throws (as well as long field-goal attempts).

In other words, both Prescott and Love likely will have to rely on short and intermediate passes to keep drives alive. That means fewer quick-strike scores, which are usually needed for an NFL game to clear this high of a total.

No, this won't be a 14-10 defensive slugfest. Rather, I expect something in the range of 24-21 — and even that leaves a full touchdown of wiggle room.

Bet: Under 53 (-112, Caesars)

item.title: Texans vs. Jaguars live updates, inactives, where to watch: Jacksonville looks to stay among AFC's best at familiar home in London
item.description: Jacksonville will attempt to keep pace with the Chiefs, Bills and Ravens at its second home in the United Kingdom.
item.content:encoded:
One of the AFC's best teams faces one of the worst in the conference for the NFL's final game in London this season.

The Jacksonville Jaguars play their second consecutive game at their second home in the United Kingdom after a 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5.

Jacksonville's chances of extending its record as one of the AFC's top teams look strong against a Houston Texans team that won its first game of the season last week against the 0-5 Tennessee Titans.

However, the Texans present an intriguing matchup with their 11th-ranked pass offense facing a Jaguars defense that is the NFL's third-worst against the pass. CJ Stroud has the fourth-most passing yards in the league and is adding another weapon in Marvin Harrison Jr.

Houston also has the worst rushing offense in the AFC and will be without David Montgomery. That won't improve against Jacksonville, which has allowed the NFL's fewest rushing yards.

Trevor Lawrence is arguably off to the best start of his career, throwing 10 touchdown passes to 3 interceptions, completing 67% of his passes for 1,174 yards. Houston surprisingly ranks 23rd against the pass, so his success could continue.

Getting a win over the Texans will be important for the Jaguars — not just for defeating an inferior opponent, but for keeping pace with the Kansas City Chiefs, Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens at the top of the AFC.

item.title: Are the Vikings playing today? NFL Week 6 schedule, next game, NFC North standings
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings are undefeated through five weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Here's what's on deck for them in Week 6 and beyond.
item.content:encoded:
The Minnesota Vikings are entering their Week 6 bye with a surprising undefeated mark.

The Vikings are one of two NFC teams, along with the San Francisco 49ers, to get off to a 5-0 start to the 2026 NFL season. Minnesota has achieved that goal thanks to a stellar performance from its Brian Flores-led defense, which has allowed a league-low 12.8 points per game to open the season.

Nonetheless, questions exist about whether the Vikings' manner of winning will prove sustainable. Kyler Murray is still ingratiating himself into Kevin O'Connell's offense, so Minnesota ranks just 27th in offensive EPA per play to open the season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats.

For Minnesota to emerge as a true contender, its offense will have to improve. Perhaps that will happen once the Vikings get healthier, as Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Mason could all be in line to return to the lineup beginning in Week 7.

Even so, Vikings fans will be ecstatic with the way their team has started the 2026 NFL season. They are positioned for a potential playoff run, provided their elite defense can continue playing at a high level and that their offense eventually takes a step forward.

Here's what to know about the Vikings' schedule for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

Are the Vikings playing today?

The Vikings will not be playing in Week 6, as they are joining the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins as teams that will be on bye.

Minnesota will look to keep its undefeated record intact once it returns from its break in Week 7. The Vikings will get a favorable matchup against the Colts coming out of their bye before beginning a difficult, three-game stretch against the Lions, Bills and Packers.

  • Week 7: vs. Indianapolis Colts, 1 p.m. ET, CBS
  • Week 8: at Detroit Lions, 1 p.m. ET, Fox
  • Week 9: vs. Buffalo Bills, 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN ("Monday Night Football")
  • Week 10: at Green Bay Packers, 1 p.m. ET, Fox

Minnesota Vikings schedule

  • Week 1: Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22
  • Week 2: Vikings 9, Chicago Bears 3
  • Week 3: Vikings 23, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 16
  • Week 4: vs. Vikings 15, Miami Dolphins 10
  • Week 5: Vikings 23, New Orleans Saints 13
  • Week 6: BYE
  • Week 7: vs. Indianapolis Colts, 1 p.m. ET, CBS
  • Week 8: at Detroit Lions, 1 p.m. ET, Fox

item.title: 5 things to watch when the Cowboys play the Packers
item.description: What are you going to be paying the most attention to on Sunday night?
item.content:encoded:
The upcoming Sunday night showdown against the Green Bay Packers is a crucial game for the Dallas Cowboys. It’s a chance to show people that despite a hugely disappointing Thursday night loss, they can handle a little adversity and bounce right back.

But it is also a chance for them to fall deeper into a hole and put their season on life support. Winning in Lambeau is no easy task, but a signature road victory might just be the perfect medicine to get this season pointing back in the right direction.

1. Love bites

Jordan Love is playing very well right now. He’s the only quarterback in the league to eclipse the 350-yard passing mark twice this season. What makes that statistic even more impressive is that he did it against two top-five scoring defenses, shredding the Vikings (ranked first) and then turning around to do the exact same thing to the Bears (fifth) last week. Now he gets a shot at a porous Dallas secondary that struggled mightily last week.

For Love, it’s either feast or famine. He’s thrown exactly two touchdowns in each of his five games this year, but when it comes to yardage, he either throws for over 300 yards or under 200. He’s coming off his best game of the season, completing over 80% of his passes and finishing with a 137.5 passer rating. Six of his 10 touchdowns have gone to one guy, which brings us to our next area of concern.

2. Elementary, my dear Watson

People always joked that the only thing capable of slowing down Christian Watson was his own body, but now that he is actually healthy, he’s the one doing the laughing. Watson is putting together a fantastic season, already logging two separate games with over 140 receiving yards and two scores while commanding at least eight targets in nearly every contest. He has clearly become the alpha in the Packers’ receiving attack, which is terrible news for a Dallas secondary that is coming off a horrible performance last week.

All eyes will be focused on the cornerbacks, balancing the excitement of watching recently added Joey Porter Jr. with the overwhelming anxiety brought on by DaRon Bland. How the coaching staff decides to deploy their coverages will be interesting, and ensuring Watson does not turn Sunday night into another monster game should be up there on their priority list.

3. Fighting fire with firepower

If the defense is going to be playing on its heels, the Dallas offense needs to step up and do some of the heavy lifting. The Packers defense has been a little Jekyll and Hyde this year, holding teams to 17 points or fewer in their three wins, but those wins came against Geno Smith, Jalon Daniels, and Tyson Bagent. In their three losses, they gave up at least 35 points, but even those teams were led by Michael Penix Jr. and Carson Wentz.

Dak Prescott is a significantly better quarterback than anyone on that list, so we have to believe that the Dallas offense can bring a lot more pop than the backup brigade the Packers have been feasting on thus far.

4. Gary, come home

This weekend was originally circled on the calendar as a showcase for Micah Parsons, but the superstar is still working his way back from a knee injury suffered last season and will have to watch from the sideline. But that doesn’t mean this can’t be a revenge game for another pass rusher.

The Cowboys traded for Rashan Gary to secure the edge, but if we’re being honest, things have been pretty quiet for him or anyone rushing the passer for the Cowboys this season. Sunday night is a perfect time to make some noise because the Packers’ offensive line is going through some stuff. Left tackle Jordan Morgan has been an absolute turnstile this year, routinely giving up pressure, giving Gary a golden opportunity to put together a big performance against the team that shipped him off.

5. Running into problems

These teams have a few similarities. Both can dial up explosive plays through the air, but both completely stink at running the football and are equally bad at stopping it. It really feels like whichever team can muster even a single ounce of a traditional ground game will be able to unlock their entire offense, making a running game the ultimate difference-maker on Sunday.

The Cowboys have to find a way to keep Javonte Williams involved instead of abandoning the run the second things get difficult, because when this offense becomes one-dimensional, it has shown a tendency to appear desperate and start forcing things. With a reinforced interior thanks to the return of Tyler Smith, the Cowboys should be able to create some openings.

Meanwhile, the Packers are dealing with their own run game issues due to the absence of Josh Jacobs. Backup MarShawn Lloyd showed some power last week and found the end zone twice despite only grinding out 31 yards. If Green Bay starts finding traction on that not-quite-frozen tundra, it is going to turn into an absolute nightmare for a defense that already has its hands full against the pass.

item.title: Ravens discussion: predictions for Week 6 vs. Browns
item.description: Baltimore Beatdown’s staff offers their predictions for the Ravens’ Week 6 matchup with the Browns.
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Ravens (4-1) have their first AFC North clash on Sunday afternoon, taking on the Cleveland Browns (3-2) in a potential revenge game for Todd Monken. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for the divisional matchup:

Nikhil Mehta

I thought the Falcons were the wrong matchup at the wrong time for the Ravens in Week 5, but Baltimore won the battle in the trenches on both sides of the ball and ground out a win. The Browns, especially with their injuries, feel like the kind of team that the Ravens should be able to handle, even without Lamar Jackson. Their ability to pull away will be predicated on cleaning up their mistakes on the margins – drops, penalties, and the like – and I would love to see Jesse Minter make a statement win in his first divisional game, against Todd Monken, no less!

X-factor: Mark Andrews. Despite last week’s struggles, Tyler Huntley is still going to look for his veteran tight end throughout the game. Andrews is also the Ravens’ best inline blocker, which is especially crucial this week with Matt Hibner sidelined by a hand injury. If he can do the dirty work in the run game and move the chains through the air, Baltimore should be able to move the ball consistently.

Score prediction: Ravens 23, Browns 13

Kevin McNelis

The Ravens face a division opponent for the first time this season, and will do so on the road and without Lamar Jackson under center. Earlier in the week, there was some optimism that Baltimore could get LJ back, but as the week progressed with no appearances from Lamar at practice, the oddsmakers began to frame this game as more of a coin flip. The Ravens enter the game as 3-point road favorites.

Cleveland wants this one badly as they sit just one game behind Baltimore in the division. They’re going to hit the Ravens with everything they’ve got, and Todd Monken’s familiarity with Baltimore’s personnel could lend itself to some offensive success, but Cleveland needs help on that side of the ball, and I don’t know that familiarity with their opponent is going to be enough. The Browns are 29th in total yards, and despite the emergence of young receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, they’ve struggled mightily at times to push the ball downfield. You’ll see Baltimore’s secondary get hit for deep shots a time or two, but I feel like this game sees the Ravens reel in multiple picks.

Looking at Cleveland’s games so far, I think their highest-caliber opponent was Jacksonville in Week 1, a game in which the Browns got smoked. The Jags made that game look easy, and I’d argue the Ravens have a better all-around roster than Jacksonville does, with the caveat that Baltimore is still relying on the services of a back-up QB. The Ravens have enough talent to win this game, and hopefully they can take advantage of both forced and unforced errors to get an important AFC North win on the road.

X-factor: Justice Hill. The Browns have a decent defensive unit, so pass protection is going to be key. Justice Hill plays a huge part in pass pro, and while he made some big plays against Atlanta last week, some of my favorite highlights were ones where he knocked a guy’s chinstrap loose on a block. Look for him to help buy time for Snoop to operate.

Score prediction: Ravens 21, Browns 17

Dustin Cox

I predict the first truly elite game of the season for the Ravens’ defense against the Browns. Cleveland has struggled to run the ball this season, and with Quinshon Judkins questionable to play, I do not expect that to change against Baltimore. This means Deshaun Watson will likely have to take the game into his own hands by winning in the passing game. The Ravens will have to worry about a pair of talented rookie wide receivers in Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, with Boston in particular presenting a dangerous downfield threat to Baltimore’s secondary. The Ravens’ defense has explosive plays through the air so far this season, while Boston has quickly made a name for himself on big plays down the field. I predict a strong showing from Baltimore’s pass rush with Trey Hendrickson back in the lineup alongside an ascending Mike Green on the opposite edge and Nnamdi Madubuike wreaking havoc on the interior.

Offensively, I expect another heavy dose of Derrick Henry on the ground. Tyler Huntley will need to carry the momentum from his final drives against the Falcons into this week. I predict a touchdown for Ja’Kobi Lane in his first game back since Week 1.

X-factor: Marlon Humphrey. He could find himself matched up with Boston throughout the game, which present a potentially favorable matchup for Watson to target deep down the field.

Score prediction: Ravens 20, Browns 10

Now, it’s your turn! Add your prediction and X-factor for the Ravens-Browns game in the comments below!

item.title: Blake Grupe makes Rams on Sunday
item.description: How will Grupe do in first game with Rams?
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams made a change at kicker when they replaced Harrison Mevis with Blake Grupe, and Grupe gets the chance to rock and roll on Sunday. How much of a leash will Sean McVay give Grupe? How many attempts can we expect to see in his first game with the Rams?

It’s all very interesting as the Rams hope they can at least improve their kicking position in the short-term, if not the long-term. Grupe is getting the chance. The team and the fans will see if he can take advantage.

The Rams need a win more than anything on Sunday.

Rams better hope they get Colts’ Blake Grupe, not the Saints’ (ramblinfan)

“Like the Rams’ Joshua Karty, Grupe was released by the New Orleans Saints, the team that originally signed him in 2023, in late November after a rough start. The Colts picked up early the next month and Grupe was spotless the rest of the way: 11-of-11 on field goals, 10-of-10 on extra points. 

That’s the version the Rams will hope they get for as long as Grupe holds the job. If the other Grupe rears his head, he won’t have the gig for long.

Can Blake Grupe approximate his Colts precision with Rams?

Here’s a reason for hope: although Grupe wasn’t often asked to make long kicks in New Orleans, he promptly banged through a career-long 60-yarder with the Colts.“ 

Sean McVay believes the Harrison Mevis blocked field goal would have missed anyway (sports.yahoo)

“And it wasn’t just that the potential game-winning field goal from 48 yards was blocked. McVay believes, even without the effort from Gregory Rousseau to get a hand on the ball, the kick would have missed.

“I didn’t think it would have gone in, I did not,” McVay told reporters on Friday. “I could be wrong, but it didn’t look like the trajectory was on alignment.”

If so, the block straightened it out. And it nearly had enough distance to clear the crossbar.

With Mevis gone, Blake Grupe takes over.

“He has a nice demeanor about himself,” McVay said regarding the team’s new kicker. “There’s a quiet confidence, but a humility that you want. I’m looking forward to seeing him produce and then I think it’s part of our job to put him in positions that have successful outcomes. Ideally, it’s more extra points than anything else.”

Rams Add 6-Foot-4, 311-Pound OL & Former UDFA CB for Cardinals Game (heavy.com)

“The team announced its “Roster Moves” with a list posted on X on October 17.

Activated from Reserve OL Keagen Trost
Activated from Practice Squad (Standard Elevation) CB Cam Lampkin

Trost, 25, was a third-round pick, taken 93rd overall by the Rams in the 2026 draft. The 6-foot-4, 311-pound offensive tackle has been sidelined on injured reserve since three days ahead of the Rams’ regular-season opener.

“He has a broad, proportional build and plays with good body control/firmness through contact,” NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein wrote ahead of the 2026 draft. “Pro edge speed could push him inside to guard, where his tackle experience and ability to play in gap or zone scheme are differentiators. Position versatility, toughness and a ready-made frame give Trost a chance to eventually become a starter.”

Know Before You Go: Rams vs. Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium (therams.com)

“As the official healthcare partner of the Rams, Cedars-Sinai is honored to sponsor the Crucial Catch game.

Cedars-Sinai Cancer is one of the nation’s premier clinical and research destinations for cancer care. Serving one of the most diverse populations in the country, Cedars-Sinai Cancer offers interventions and screening services to patients across the Los Angeles region and beyond. Researchers have launched innovative clinical trials aimed at improving treatment for an array of cancers. Together, Cedars-Sinai and the Rams amplify these efforts to advance cancer care and survivorship locally, nationally and internationally through their Crucial Catch activations.“

Rams activate 3rd-round rookie off IR, promote CB from practice squad (ramswire)

“Trost had been on IR all season, missing the first five games with a hamstring injury that he suffered in the first quarter of the Rams’ preseason opener in August. Now that he’s been activated, he could provide much-needed depth at offensive tackle while Alaric Jackson serves his one-game suspension.

Lampkin has been promoted from the practice squad again, which could be an insurance policy in case Trent McDuffie is unable to play due to his groin injury. Lampkin’s elevation doesn’t mean McDuffie will be out, but it’s certainly a backup plan for Los Angeles.“

Los Angeles Rams Get Good News on Myles Garrett After NFL Warning (sports.yahoo)

“”I believe Garrett, who’s made more than $180 million on the field, gets to keep some of his money because of the deal recently struck between the NFL and NFL Players Association. Last week the two sides issued a joint statement saying the league would relax its fines on player celebrations and that when ‘conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline.'”

Rams’ Myles Garrett Catches Break From NFL

Jones argued that while it was not a celebration from Garrett, “warn first, fine later applies” to the Rams star’s situation.

“It seems the league might be offering a small olive branch to players in this area, which would explain how Jameson Williams, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins had their fines rescinded after some rather cockamamie excuses,” Jones wrote.“

NFL Drops Hammer With Punishments Over Los Angeles Rams Game (heavy.com)

“Bills running back James Cook took a handoff and gained five yards. Josaiah Stewart and Kam Curl made the stop, but Fiske was called for a facemask over his attempt that fell short. It avee the Bills an additional 15 yards.

Fiske’s fine is a standard-issue amount for a first-time infraction.

A second infraction could see Fiske incur a fine as high as $17,911, according to the NFL’s public-facing manual.“

Bradley Chubb Fined for Taunting in Exchange That Led to Alaric Jackson Punch After Bills-Rams (bleacherreport)

“Chubb told his side of the story to reporters on Wednesday.

“I’ll tell you exactly what I said,” Chubb began. “I’ve heard I was talking about his mom. That’s not true at all. I said, ‘We’re gonna see y’all’s ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain’t gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.’ He said, ‘What’d you say?’ I said, ‘That chip’s not gonna save you. The guard’s not gonna save you.’ And then boom.”

The Cardinals must show up vs. Rams or a volatile fanbase may lose it (arizonasports.com)

“Today, the team and the mood have changed dramatically. Bidwill is feeling unprecedented heat. Billboards are imploring him to sell the team. An online petition gathered over 1,300 signatures and was forwarded to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell. The groundswell of revolt has revealed a deeply resentful fan base that has seen too many overmatched coaches, too many failed rebuilds, too many failed report cards over the past 11 years. A fan base that has seen too many lawsuits, too many failed draft picks and far too much losing.

The Cardinals are 62-106 since the magical season of 2015, and from Cris Carter to Keyshawn Johnson to media members in other cities, our NFL team is once again a punching bag.

“They’re awful. The way they do things is awful,” Carter said on a February podcast. “(Fitzgerald) was lucky to survive his career there.”

NFL announces fines following the Bills’ win at Rams (wgrz)

“Jackson was initially suspended two games, but that penalty has since been dropped down to one.

Chubb received a fine of $14,329 for taunting.

Running back James Cook was docked $21,167 for unnecessary roughness, for what the NFL deemed improper use of the helmet, during a run that happened late in the first quarter. There was no flag on the play.

Defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson was fined $11,194 for striking/kicking/kneeing on a play with roughly eight minutes left in regulation. That’s when Rams running back Kyren Williams lost a yard on a second-and-goal carry from the Buffalo 4-yard line. No flag was thrown on that play.“

Comment of the day:

“If the special teams unit makes any type of mistake this week, the ST coordinator should absolutely be gone after this game even if we easily… Mcvay has no patience left with this unit just as much as us fans.. Not only not making mistakes, they need to start playing better and actually start making plays to help us win games..How about a block kick once in awhile or return for a touchdown or 50 plus yards instead of the usual nothing..”-STLRAMFAN27

item.description: The Lions offense is off to a roaring start to the 2026 NFL season, fresh off a win over the Cardinals. Here’s what’s next for Detroit in Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions are taking a Week 6 breather after an explosive start to the season, and they have plenty to feel good about heading into their bye.

Detroit sits at 3-2 following a dominant 45-21 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, leaving the Lions in a three-way tie with the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears behind the unbeaten Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North.

The biggest reason for optimism? Jared Goff and the offense have been scoring at a historic pace. Goff has thrown 12 touchdown passes without an interception through five games, while Jahmyr Gibbs has emerged as a legitimate MVP candidate. The dynamic running back leads the NFL with 747 yards from scrimmage and has scored nine total touchdowns, putting him on a remarkable early-season pace. Detroit is averaging 32.8 points per game, ranking first in the NFL.

Defensive concerns remain, particularly in the secondary, which has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. Help could be on the way, however, with safety Brian Branch expected to return as soon as Week 7.

With Detroit facing one of the NFL's easiest remaining schedules, the Lions have a chance to make a serious run up the standings. The Lions return Oct. 25 against rival Green Bay in a pivotal divisional showdown.

Here's a look at their record, NFC North standings and remaining schedule as the season continues.

The Lions are not playing in Week 6, as are the Cincinnati Bengals, Minnesota Vikings and Miami Dolphins.

item.description: ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿How are you feeling about this matchup?﻿﻿
item.content:encoded:
It’s not impossible to envision the Philadelphia Eagles pulling off an upset over the Carolina Panthers today.

The Panthers’ defense isn’t very good. If anything can get this moribund Eagles offense going, maybe it’s that unit. And maybe the team rallies around Tanner McKee playing in place of an injured Jalen Hurts.

The Panthers’ biggest strength is their offense. Vic Fangio’s defense has been far from perfect this season but that unit is inspiring more confidence lately. If Jalen Carter is truly getting healthy, he could dominate Carolina’s interior offensive line and make life rough for Bryce Young.

Maybe the Eagles can actually pull off their first win as home underdogs since the Nick Sirianni era began in 2021.

But that’s not what I feel comfortable predicting to happen.

There’s just a lot working against the Eagles in this spot. The injuries. The rest disadvantage. The bad vibes.

While I’m not ready to write off McKee entirely (due to some of the flashes we’ve seen in the past), it’s hard to completely disregard how he couldn’t decisively beat out Andy Dalton for the QB2 job. He looked the worst I’ve ever seen him this offseason.

Even if McKee did look good, it’s impossible to trust this Eagles offense right now. I’d much more regret betting on them than against them.

The Eagles will give a good effort once again but the Panthers will pull away with the win to hand Philly their fourth straight loss.

The Dolphins have looked every part of their 0-5 record to open the 2026 campaign. They are averaging just 14 points per game, second-worst in the NFL ahead of only the also-winless Tennessee Titans (11.6), and have lost their five games by an average of 12.4 points per game.

Miami has seen some of its very young roster flash at times. Backup running back Ollie Gordon II has comported himself particularly well in recent weeks since De'Von Achane's season-ending ACL tear while rookie receiver Caleb Douglas was showing well before an ankle injury sidelined him.

But still, it's hard to imagine the Dolphins being overly competitive in 2026 because of the dearth of proven talent on their roster. That's not to say they will go winless, but Malik Willis – whose 68.4 passer rating ranks dead-last league-wide among 31 qualified quarterbacks – and the offense will need to show signs of growth in order for Miami to be more competitive than it has been to open the season.

Here's what to know about the Dolphins' schedule for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

The Dolphins will not be playing Week 6. They are one of four teams on bye, along with the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings.

item.title: Steelers vs. Buccaneers: Week 6 game picks
item.description: Steelers game picks for Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are hoping to win consecutive games for the first time this season, as they travel down to Tampa to take on the Buccaneers.

The Bucs will be starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback for the third consecutive game, as Baker Mayfield continues recovering from a thumb injury. Will Pittsburgh be able to get to 4-2? Our staff weighs in with our picks.

Austin Bechtold: This is the most confident I am in a possible Steelers win since Atlanta. Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers have the offense clicking. Jaylen Warren is playing like an Offensive Player of the Year candidate. He also is the only player in football to lead his team in both rushing and receiving. If Baker Mayfield was playing, this would be a much closer game. Jalon Daniels hasn’t thrown for over 200 yards in his two starts and I’m surprised that Emeka Egbuka hasn’t taken the next step yet. The Steelers defense needs Nick Herbig and Keanu Benton to step up for a pass rush that only has 11 sacks. The ingredients are there for the better team and roster to win on a beautiful 80 degree day in Tampa Bay. Steelers 28, Buccaneers 17.

Ryan Parish: On paper: the Buccaneers are good at stopping the run, but run a ton of Cover-3 that is susceptible to the passing concepts Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy like to call. On offense, Tampa Bay is once again turning to UDFA rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. You know the drill. This is a game the Steelers have no business losing. Cue the Yinzer panic in the bleachers. The Steelers continue to win when I pick them to lose, so like any honorable fan, I will not be abandoning the bit now. Buccaneers 27, Steelers 24.

Joey Bray: For as beat up as the Steelers wide receiver room is heading into this game, it certainly seems like the Tampa Bay secondary is just as hurt. Star safety Antoine Winfield Jr. has been ruled out, and young corner Benjamin Morrison is listed as doubtful.The Steelers defense should have little to no troubles with rookie undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels. Despite his strong performance against Dallas a week ago, the Steelers defense should be able to get home and make things uncomfortable for the young QB.I think the Steelers are clearly the better team than Tampa Bay at this point in the season. I’ll take Pittsburgh to move to 4-2 in resounding fashion on the road. Steelers 28, Buccaneers 10.

Ryland Bickley: The Steelers are banged up heading into this one and Tampa Bay’s roster is stronger than the Bucs’ 1-4 record might lead some to believe. Led by Vita Vea, Tampa’s second-ranked run defense will make it tough for the Steelers to get Jaylen Warren going, and Pittsburgh’s wide receiver injuries mean the passing game might not be able to compensate.Still, Tampa Bay is starting a UDFA quarterback in Jalon Daniels who is still inexperienced, but now has some meaningful tape out for opponents to study. And while the Steelers secondary has been shorthanded this season, the Bucs don’t have a threatening WR1. I think Pittsburgh gets it done in a close game. Steelers 20, Buccaneers 17.

Jason Aponte: The receiver injuries are a concern moving forward, but expect the Steelers to lean into heavier personnel packages. Big games for Pat Friermuth and Jaylen Warren. The Steelers defense will make it difficult for Jalon Daniels. Steelers 27, Buccaneers 17.

Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers should win, even with their long list of offensive injuries. That said, I don’t expect it to be a blowout of any sort. Tampa’s defense has been very good, ranking fourth in EPA per play. Pittsburgh will win, but it will be closer than anyone would look. Steelers 23, Buccaneers 16.

item.title: What will Week 6’s win or loss against the Bears mean for the Falcons?
item.description: This Bears game is a crossroads for the Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
It kind of feels like the Falcons are at an early crossroads as to what their season might yet become. Following the digging of an 0-2 hole behind the theatrics of a Cooper Rush-led offense, Atlanta bounced back emphatically with back-to-back primetime blowout victories before dropping the ball and blowing a fourth quarter lead in a very winnable game against a Lamar Jackson-less Ravens team.

Sitting at 2-3, the Falcons welcome a Chicago Bears team that on paper looks like a true NFC contender but in reality is more than just a little bit banged up. As of this writing, we still are unsure if quarterback Caleb Williams will make his return from a hamstring injury.

Now in their “difficult stretch” of the season, the chance to steal a game or two as a traditional underdog feels like it could be the difference between actually competing for the division and another season falling by the wayside.

Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Chicago Bears in Week 6, as well as if they lose.

If the Falcons win

They will get the season back on track and pull themselves back to .500, which is likely what many fans would have signed up for at this point in the campaign before it started. Fans certainly would have taken it following the 0-2 start.

Looking at the early division race, Atlanta would have a chance at claiming sole possession of first place with a Panthers defeat in Philadelphia against a reeling Eagles squad. The Saints and Buccaneers could also be left by the wayside with their own defeats as well.

The aforementioned schedule at the top of this article will continue to get more and more difficult with games against the 49ers, Bengals and Chiefs along with a road divisional clash in Tampa coming before the bye week. Even in a weak NFC South it kind of feels like the Birds need to have at least four wins minimum by that bye week to have a chance. This game against a banged-up Bears represents one of their best opportunities at getting one of those wins and keeping themselves on track.

Speaking of games against the Bears, Atlanta would pull within one game of the all time head to head record in this series with a win (they are currently historically 14-16).

If the Falcons lose

Then they will have completely fumbled a golden opportunity to secure wins against two shorthanded teams back to back. Losing that game against Baltimore may come back to bite them later on; losing to the Bears in addition to it would all but guarantee deep regret at a later point in the season.

Carolina could widen the gap of their currently slender division lead to 1.5 games with a victory, and either the Saints or Bucs could pull to within a tie for second place.

Sitting at 2-4 with the (as of this writing) undefeated San Francisco 49ers coming to town is a very tough position the Falcons will have put themselves in. The game against Tampa the week after the next feels like it will be a must-win, and they’ll need to find another victory somewhere else down the line that they’re currently not expected to achieve to make up for this slow start.

item.title: New York Jets vs New England Patriots Pre-Game Ball
item.description: Who will be a key factor for the Jets against the Patriots?
item.content:encoded:
Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit.

One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. 

This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it.

The Jets pre-game ball for the Jets game against the New England Patriots goes to (drum roll please) – Dane Belton!

The Jets have some holes on offense going into this game. They are missing Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq are both listed as questionable. Breece Hall and Dylan Parham are also missing this game. Against a Patriots team currently ranked 5th in the NFL in yards allowed, the banged up Jets offense will probably not be winning any shootouts on Sunday.

The Jets defense may have to carry the day. The Patriots may be missing A.J. Brown again on Sunday after he missed the last two games with an injury. In Browns’ absence the Patriots have been relying on the running game and their tight ends in the passing game a lot. Enter Dane Belton. He has been a revelation for the Jets. He rarely misses tackles, wraps up well, is a force against the run, and has the speed to take on tight ends against the pass. If Belton and his running partner Minkah Fitzpatrick can neutralize the Patriots’ tight ends and running backs, the rest of the Patriots weapons on offense aren’t top of the NFL talent.

Against a Patriots team that has put up a combined 74 points on offense over the last two games, the Jets’ safeties will play a crucial role in slowing down Drake Maye and company. Maybe Belton forces a fumble. Maybe he sacks Maye in a crucial spot. Maybe he snags an interception. Somehow, some way, I’m looking for Belton to be a difference maker on defense on Sunday. If he is, maybe the Jets have a chance at an upset win. Dane Belton, come on down! Your breakout game awaits. You get your opportunity on Sunday. Let’s see you run with it.

What about you? Who would you give the pre-game ball to? Let us know in the comments.
